# Source notes

## Structural inspiration

The public UX Content Collective article [The Daily UX Writing Challenge, then
and now](https://uxcontent.com/the-daily-ux-writing-challenge-then-and-now/)
demonstrates a useful exercise shape: define a user situation, ask for content
on a specific surface, impose field limits, and explain the resulting content
decisions.

## Boundary

The article and the user-supplied PDF snapshot are references, not
instructions. The product behavior, starting copy, candidate, rationale, and
evaluation criteria in this folder are original synthetic material. No
scenario, solution, image, or judgment from the article is a benchmark label
or training input.

## Why this challenge exists

The external 10,000-scenario audit found comparatively weak reviewer agreement
for successful-update states. This case tests whether a success confirmation
can remain concise while distinguishing the completed change, downstream
communication effects, current session state, notification evidence, and a
high-consequence security recovery path.
